overview.text: The Blunthead Tree Snake is an extremely thin tree snake of Mexico, Central and South America, with a big head and huge eyes. It has a very mild venom and is harmless to people.

identification.text: A long, very slender body - like a fiddle string - with a large, blunt head and big eyes.

size.label: Adults
size.text: About 80 cm long on average, up to about 1.5 m.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: Eastern Mexico through Central America to South America as far as Bolivia, Paraguay and northern Argentina, and Trinidad and Tobago.

habitat.text: Cool, moist forests and rainforests, from sea level to about 1,700 m; often in low plants such as coffee bushes and bromeliads.

behaviour.text: Active at night, searching through thick vegetation; by day it rests coiled in deep shade.

recognise.text: Extremely thin body with a big head.
